properties.name: unbounded parameter domain
properties.example: a property of the acting group, not of the geometry; true in every example below

properties.name: compact orbit closure
properties.definition: the closure of {Φ_t(x)} in the state space X is compact

properties.name: unbounded lift
properties.definition: the orbit lifted to the universal cover of X is unbounded
properties.example: θ(t) = ωt on the cover ℝ → S¹ (A8Cf); trivial on simply connected X (ℝ², intervals)

properties.name: bounded observable
properties.definition: a stated observable (here the ambient Euclidean coordinates) stays bounded for all t

properties.name: infinitely many cycles
properties.definition: the full state completes infinitely many periods: non-constant periodic orbit, N(t) = ⌊t/T⌋ → ∞
properties.example: circle (A8Cd); a fixed point completes no cycle

properties.name: convergence
properties.definition: lim_(t→+∞) Φ_t(x) exists in the ambient space

properties.name: periodicity
properties.definition: Φ_T(x) = x for some T > 0 (Stab(x) ≠ {0}; fixed points included)

properties.name: dense orbit
properties.definition: the orbit closure is all of X
properties.example: irrational torus (Kronecker, A8Tb); also the logistic orbit (0, 1) in [0, 1]

properties.name: noncompact drift
properties.definition: the forward orbit leaves every compact subset of X

implications: compact orbit closure ⇒ bounded (any continuous observable)
taxonomy.note: "Infinite" is no longer used without naming the object: the parameter domain, the lift, the cycle count and the orbit length can be unbounded while the image is compact. "Bounded" depends on the chosen observable and metric: the velocity orbit is bounded in v and unbounded in the rapidity artanh v, which is a topological conjugacy (A8Pg); compactness of the orbit closure does not depend on that choice.

circle.statement: Φ_t(z) = e^(iωt)z is a one-parameter group action of (ℝ, +) on S¹: Φ_0 = id, Φ_t∘Φ_s = Φ_(t+s); |γ_ω(t)| = 1 for every real t
for ω ≠ 0 the minimal positive period is T = 2π/|ω|
for ω ≠ 0, lim_(t→∞) cos ωt and sin ωt do not exist; both stay in [−1, 1]: the old wording "sines and cosines converge to infinity" is FALSE
t, the phase lift θ = ωt and the cycle count N(t) are unbounded; the image is the compact S¹, reached in one period
Stab(z) = Tℤ for every z (Stab = ℝ when ω = 0); the orbit map induces ℝ/Tℤ ≅ S¹, and with p(σ) = e^(2πiσ), γ_ω(t) = p(ωt/2π): ℝ/Tℤ ≅ ℝ/ℤ ≅ S¹ by t ↦ ωt/2π (T ↦ ±1)

p: ℝ → S¹ is a covering map (fibres σ + ℤ, deck translations, local diffeomorphism); the lift of γ_ω is σ(t) = ωt/2π. The unbounded object is the covering coordinate; S¹ is compact and is not called infinite

circleNote: The acting parameter is ℝ; the orbit/image geometry is S¹. The finite/infinite relation is exact: an unbounded covering parameter represents a compact periodic geometry because points separated by the period are identified (the quotient ℝ/Tℤ). Nothing about the circle converges.

torus.statement: (e^(iω_1t), …, e^(iω_nt)) is periodic ⟺ ∃T > 0 with Tω_j ∈ 2πℤ for all j ⟺ (for ω ≠ 0) all ratios ω_j/ω_k are rational (commensurable); minimal period T/2π = lcm(b_j)/gcd(a_j) for ω_j = a_j/b_j > 0
(1, √2): Stab = {0} at every point (the orbit map ℝ → T² is injective); the orbit is dense in T² (Kronecker; checked: 400 section returns come within 0.016 of every grid point)
torus.status: PROVED (stabilizer); density: known theorem, source-locked, numerical instance carded

torus.statement: near-recurrence is not periodicity: distances 2|sin(π√2q)| at continued-fraction denominators decrease below 0.01 and are never 0
rationally dependent but not commensurable, (1, √2, 1 + √2): relation lattice ℤ(1, 1, −1), the orbit lies in the 2-dimensional subtorus z₃ = z₁z₂ (dense there by Kronecker), not periodic
torus.status: PROVED (confinement); density on the subtorus: source-locked

torus.statement: compact/constrained image ⇏ exact periodic orbit: on T² the (1, √2) flow preserves |z₁| = |z₂| = 1, has no fixed point and NO periodic orbit at all
the orbit-closure dimension is n − rank(integer relation lattice of ω): the frequency vector's arithmetic decides the behaviour; the torus and its invariants are identical in every case
torus.status: PROVED for the examples; the general statement is the Kronecker–Weyl theorem (source-locked)

cylinder.statement: Φ_t(z, x) = (e^(iωt)z, x + vt) on S¹ × ℝ, v ≠ 0: the angular projection is periodic (period 2π/|ω|); the full state has Stab = {0}; x(t) is unbounded; the orbit leaves every compact set (not recurrent)
a periodic state makes every observable periodic; a periodic observable (Re z) does not make the state periodic (x(t + T) − x(t) = 2πv/ω ≠ 0)

cylinderNote: One unbounded parameter drives a bounded periodic projection and an unbounded coordinate at the same time. Periodicity of a representation/projection is a different property from periodicity of the full state.

definitions: one-parameter action: a continuous map Φ: ℝ × X → X on a Hausdorff (here metric) space X with Φ_0 = id and Φ_t∘Φ_s = Φ_(t+s)
orbit: O(x) = {Φ_t(x) : t ∈ ℝ}; forward orbit: t ≥ 0
stabilizer: Stab(x) = {t ∈ ℝ : Φ_t(x) = x}, a subgroup of ℝ; it is closed because it is the preimage of the point x under the continuous map t ↦ Φ_t(x) into a Hausdorff space
framework.theorem: Stab(x) ∈ {ℝ, Tℤ (T > 0), {0}}. Proof: a closed subgroup H ≠ {0} has τ = inf(H ∩ (0, ∞)); if τ = 0, H contains arbitrarily small positive elements, so it is dense and, being closed, H = ℝ; if τ > 0, τ ∈ H (closed) and every h ∈ H lies in τℤ (division with remainder). The dense subgroup ℤ + √2ℤ is not closed and is never a stabilizer (A8Pa).

classes.name: periodic
classes.condition: Stab(x) = Tℤ; T is the minimal period and the orbit is homeomorphic to ℝ/Tℤ ≅ S¹ (continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space)
classes.example: circle, rational torus, rotation of ℝ²

classes.name: free, compact orbit closure, recurrent ("aperiodic recurrent"; quasi-periodic is the torus-linear-flow example of it)
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; forward orbit closure compact; Φ_(t_n)(x) → x for some t_n → ∞

classes.name: free, compact orbit closure, not recurrent
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; closure compact; no return near x
classes.example: logistic orbit converging to fixed points; θ̇ = 1 − cos θ on S¹

classes.name: free, drift
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; the forward orbit leaves every compact subset of X
classes.example: cylinder, translation on ℝ, the velocity flow on (−1, 1) (boundary approach)

classes.name: free, noncompact closure, not escaping
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; closure noncompact but the orbit returns to some compact set for arbitrarily large t
classes.example: none carded in this pass; kept as a class

framework.exhaustive: The stabilizer trichotomy is logically exhaustive (theorem above). The sub-classes of free orbits come from two dichotomies (orbit closure compact or not; recurrent or not, resp. escaping or not), so the six classes are exhaustive as a decision tree; the named examples are known examples, not an exhaustive classification for this project.
terminology: "periodic" only for Stab = Tℤ (or fixed points when stated); an irrational torus flow is never called periodic
"quasi-periodic" only for linear flows on tori with rationally independent frequencies (or functions of such flows), not for every bounded non-periodic orbit
"recurrent" = positively recurrent (x lies in its own ω-limit set); near return ≠ exact return
"drift" = escapes every compact set; "boundary approach" is drift in an open state space that converges in an ambient space (A8Pg)
Poincaré recurrence is a measure statement: invariant measure, finite total measure, almost every point (A8Pd); it is not implied by compactness alone
framework.explains: It explains which behaviour occurs from objects the system supplies: the stabilizer (from the action), the orbit closure and recurrence (from the action and the topology of X). Unboundedness of the parameter is common to every row of the distinction table and decides nothing (A8Da).

star.name: forced periodicity
star.words: A constrained geometry forces every admissible evolution to be periodic.
star.verdict: FAIL. Compact T² with preserved invariants |z₁| = |z₂| = 1 and the (1, √2) flow has no periodic orbit at all (A8X1); compact [0, 1] with the logistic flow has no periodic non-fixed orbit (A8X3). Rejected: compact geometry ⇒ periodicity (A8Ra).

star.name: existence
star.words: A constrained geometry admits at least one periodic evolution.
star.verdict: RESTRICTED. If fixed points count as periodic, the claim is vacuous: every space carries Φ_t = id (A8Pe). For a non-constant periodic orbit the answer depends on the class: flows on ℝ or an interval have none (orbits are monotone; a continuous injection ℝ/Tℤ → ℝ is impossible), the circle has them, and every smooth manifold of dimension ≥ 2 admits one (a rotation field in a coordinate disk multiplied by a bump function; the local model is A8X4; this general construction is a project argument, not carded). "Bound by rules" does not decide it; the topology of the space and the admissible class of dynamics do.

star.name: recurrence
star.words: Compact/constrained geometry tends to produce recurrence or near return.
star.verdict: RESTRICTED to the Poincaré recurrence theorem (known; PROVED under its hypotheses): an invariant measure, finite total measure, conclusion for almost every point. Each hypothesis is needed (A8Pd): infinite measure (cylinder) — no point recurs; Lebesgue not invariant (logistic) — no interior point recurs; on compact S¹ with θ̇ = 1 − cos θ the only invariant probability is δ₀ and every other orbit is non-recurrent. Topological recurrence (some recurrent point exists on a compact metric space — a minimal set, Birkhoff) is a separate, weaker statement, source-only here.

cFamily.statement: M_c = diag(1, −1/c²) = P_cᵀηP_c, P_c = diag(1, 1/c), η = diag(1, −1); q_c = t² − x²/c²; for finite c₁, c₂, SᵀM_(c₂)S = M_(c₁) with S = diag(1, c₂/c₁): finite-c congruence / representation normalization only
finite c > 0: det = −1/c², rank 2, eigenvalues {1, −1/c²}, signature (1, 1), inverse diag(1, −c²)

null cone x = ±ct; null directions (1, ±c)/√(1 + c²) → (0, ±1); in x̃ = x/c every finite-c cone is x̃ = ±t. Changing coordinates inside one finite-c theory moves the cone's slope; changing c across the family is a different operation, and only the family reaches the limit

cFamilyNote: Not inferred: that physical c is meaningless. The congruence says only that, inside one theory, the value of c is fixed by the choice of spatial unit; the invariant content of the family is whether c is finite (A8Mc, A8Lc).

cLimit.statement: M_c → M_∞ = diag(1, 0): a degenerate bilinear form (rank 1, det 0, eigenvalues {1, 0}, signature (+, 0)); no inverse; M_c⁻¹ diverges while c⁻²M_c⁻¹ → h = diag(0, −1); M_∞ = ττᵀ with τ = dt and hτ = 0. P_c → diag(1, 0) is singular and det(PᵀηP) = −det(P)² ≠ 0 for invertible P: no change of coordinates reaches M_∞. M_∞ is not called "the Newtonian metric": it is one degenerate form; Galilean / Newton–Cartan-type structure also needs the cometric h (Malament 2012, source-locked) and more
the null set of M_∞ is the single line t = 0 (a double root)
preservation group of M_∞: A = [[±1, 0], [k, d]], d ≠ 0 — a 2-parameter identity component including spatial dilations; it is NOT automatically the Galilean group; also preserving h forces d = ±1
Lorentz boost t′ = γ_c(t − vx/c²), x′ = γ_c(x − vt): ΛᵀM_cΛ = M_c, det 1, rapidity group law, relativistic velocity addition
fixed finite v: γ_c → 1, t′ → t, x′ → x − vt, v₁ ⊕ v₂ → v₁ + v₂ (the Galilean boost limit); the Galilean boost preserves M_∞ and h

group contraction (İnönü–Wigner): [K_c, H] = −P, [K_c, P] = −H/c², [H, P] = 0; derived algebra dimension 2 for every finite c and 1 at c = ∞, so Poincaré(1+1) ≇ Galilei(1+1), while all finite c are isomorphic (K′ = cK, P′ = cP)

form degeneration (M_c → M_∞) and group contraction (Lorentz → Galilean boosts) are related but not identical: the limit form's preservation group (2 parameters) is larger than the contracted boost group (1 parameter); the contraction is a statement about generators and structure constants
c → ∞ with β = v/c fixed (and x̃ = x/c): no limit in (t, x), nothing changes in (t, x̃): no contraction and no rank loss. "c → ∞" has content only once what is held fixed is stated

sixQuestions.question: Does finite c function as an invariant rule inside Lorentzian geometry?
sixQuestions.answer: YES (A8La): c fixes the preserved form M_c, the null cone x = ±ct and the boost group; known mathematics and physics

sixQuestions.question: Does varying c give a meaningful family of geometries/forms?
sixQuestions.answer: YES in fixed units (t, x) (A8Ma, A8Md), but every finite member is congruent to η: inside one theory the value of c is a unit choice; the family's invariant content is finiteness (A8Mc, A8Lc)

sixQuestions.question: Does c → ∞ produce a singular/degenerate limit?
sixQuestions.answer: YES with v and x fixed: the rank drops from 2 to 1, the limit lies outside every congruence class, and the algebra contracts (A8Mc, A8Lc); the drop need not occur under another scaling: NO with β = v/c fixed (A8X5)

sixQuestions.question: Is that structurally the same phenomenon as t ∈ ℝ ↦ e^(iωt) ∈ S¹?
sixQuestions.answer: NO (A8Sa, A8Sb): an external family parameter drifting to a degenerate boundary point, not an internal action wrapping onto a compact orbit

sixQuestions.question: If not the same, is there a narrower common categorical/geometric statement?
sixQuestions.answer: YES, restricted: both examples are one-parameter subgroups preserving a quadratic form, with t ↔ rapidity s and r ↔ c (A8Sb); and both c and the circle family are orbits of one-parameter groups (on different spaces: S¹ vs Sym(2)) with opposite behaviour classes

sixQuestions.question: If even that is too weak, record the negative result.
sixQuestions.answer: Recorded: the H3 wrapping mechanism does not transfer to c (FAIL as same construction); "c converges to infinity like t" is SUPERFICIAL. The surviving correspondence is the known CF1/S4 object, not a new H3 structure

rolesLink: H3-1 (the two roles of c), restricted answer: Role 2 (c fixes the invariant form) and Role 3 (c → ∞) are roles of the same form constant. At finite c the value of c is not an isomorphism invariant (all finite-c forms are congruent and all finite-c algebras isomorphic); what is invariant is finiteness: M_c is nondegenerate and the algebra is Poincaré exactly when c < ∞ (A8Ma, A8Mc, A8Lc). This is known mathematics; it does not by itself make c an instance of the circle mechanism.
